chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Abū Ayyūb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
There has not been, in what has passed, nor in what remains, nor in that which you are in, any believer except that he has a neighbor who harms him.

key_terms.جَارٌ: a neighbor; one living nearby with social proximity
key_terms.مَا بَقِيَ: what remains; the future time yet to come
key_terms.مَا مَضَى: what has passed; the past ages
key_terms.مُؤْمِنٌ: a believer; one characterized by iman
key_terms.يُؤْذِيهِ: harms him; causes him hurt or annoyance

ai.seo_question: Does every believer face harm from neighbors as part of their trial?
ai.summary: This hadith states that hardship from neighbors is a recurring reality in the life of the believer across times. It highlights patience as part of the believer’s trial and frames social harm as something long associated with iman.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abu Ayoub, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It has not been in the past, nor in what remains (of the future), nor in (the time) what you are in, any Momin except that there is a neighbour for him troubling him’.
en.sarwar: 12. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from abu Ayyub from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
In the past, in future and in your time there has never been a believer, whom a neighbor did not make suffer.”
